extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, policymakers, and activists interested in industrial disasters and chemical safety
extracted.subtask_description: A detailed Wikipedia-style article documenting the causes, corporate and regulatory failures, human and environmental impacts, legal aftermath, remediation, activism, and cultural responses to the Bhopal gas disaster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational safety systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety systems must be functioning — the article notes that "most of the safety systems were not functioning on the night of 3 December 1984."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect multistage automated systems with reliable manual backups; anti-patterns include relying on single manual backups or letting alarms/backups be inoperable for years (the MIC tank alarms had not been working for four years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate maintenance and repair
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment and instruments must be properly maintained — e.g., MIC tank pressure gauge had been malfunctioning for roughly a week and other devices were out of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace or repair faulty instrumentation promptly rather than using ad-hoc workarounds; avoid using other tanks/systems as substitutes instead of fixing root causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate safety-audit frequency and follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety audits should be regular and followed up — the page contrasts yearly audits in US/EU plants with audits every two years elsewhere and notes a 1982 audit listing 61 hazards with no sustained follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure audits are frequent enough for the risk profile, that follow-up teams act on findings, and that temporary fixes become permanent; anti-pattern: not sending follow-up teams and letting conditions re-deteriorate by 1984.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient staffing and trained operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate numbers of skilled operators and supervisors are required — by 1984 staffing and supervisory levels had been reduced (six of original 12 MIC operators remained; supervisory personnel halved, no maintenance supervisor on night shift).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain required shift supervision, proper handover practices, and training; anti-patterns include understaffing, reduced supervision, and operating with fewer qualified staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment and resourcing for safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Underinvestment in safety (cost-cutting, halted promotions, fewer training resources) degrades safety culture and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for maintenance, training, and safety-critical spare parts; avoid cost-cuts that remove redundant safety layers or force use of inappropriate language manuals, lowering morale and safety compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design standards and material suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant design and material choices must suit chemical hazards — e.g., use of carbon steel valves that corrode when exposed to acid was inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use corrosion-resistant materials and design to industry best-practices; avoid "Indianized" downgrades that sacrifice safety for using local materials without equivalent performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate emergency action plans and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be established action plans for accidents, and local authorities must be informed of quantities and dangers — the plant had no plans to cope with accidents of this magnitude and failed to inform local authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain documented catastrophe management plans, local notification procedures, evacuation protocols and drills; anti-patterns: no action plans and inadequate notification to first responders and communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct and complete cleaning/isolating procedures (slip-blind plates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical isolation measures (e.g., slip-blind plates) must be installed and included in cleaning checklists — these were not installed and had been omitted from the cleaning checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include isolation hardware in standard operating procedures and checklists; anti-pattern: omitting critical isolation steps from cleaning procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate auxiliary control systems (deluge guns, water pressure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Auxiliary mitigation systems such as deluge guns must be capable of reaching and neutralizing escaping gas — water pressure was too weak to spray high enough to reduce gas concentrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and test auxiliary systems to reach design targets under realistic conditions; anti-pattern: underpowered or nonfunctional mitigation equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper temperature control for hazardous storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Storage conditions must follow recommended temperature controls — MIC was kept at 20°C instead of the 4.5°C advised by the manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor and maintain prescribed storage temperatures continuously; anti-patterns: idling refrigeration to save costs and thereby increasing reaction risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient flare tower and scrubber capacity and uptime
rubrics_metrics.description: Gas treatment and venting infrastructure must have capacity and be operational — the flare tower could handle only a quarter of leaked gas and several scrubbers were out of service for months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure treatment units are sized for credible worst-case releases and kept in service; anti-pattern: leaving major abatement systems out of service for long periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumentation and monitoring reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruments (e.g., pressure gauges) must be reliable — missing or malfunctioning indicators precluded timely detection (gauge malfunction, missing local pressure indicator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement redundancy, regular calibration, and prompt repairs; anti-pattern: operating with known faulty instruments for extended periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent, independent incident investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations should be open and allow access — the article reports that government denied UCC investigators access to the tank and operator interviews were restricted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable independent investigators full access to sites, logs, and personnel; anti-pattern: controlling investigations to limit evidence or exclude parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity of records and logfiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurate, unaltered operational records are required — the page cites allegations and graphological analysis showing attempts to alter logfiles and destroy log evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect logs, apply tamper-evident measures, retain backups, and support forensic review; anti-pattern: log alteration, deletion, or poor record retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical security and controls to prevent sabotage
rubrics_metrics.description: Access controls should prevent deliberate introduction of hazardous materials — sabotage hypothesis alleges an employee connected a water hose through a metering port.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure metering ports, lock out physical access to critical tank connections, control inventory of hoses and tools; anti-pattern: unsecured access points enabling malicious acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waste management and site remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandoned chemicals must be managed and the site remediated — chemicals abandoned at the plant continued to leak and pollute groundwater and soil for decades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform thorough remediation, long-term monitoring, safe disposal, and transparent reporting; anti-patterns: using plant as dumping ground and delaying cleanup for decades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental monitoring against health-based standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Soil, groundwater, and biological monitoring should be compared to recognized safety limits (WHO, EPA) — samples showed contaminants exceeding WHO/EPA limits by orders of magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accredited labs, measure against international/national standards, and publish results; anti-pattern: lack of systematic testing or ignoring exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory oversight and information-sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulators must enforce standards and share important safety findings between facilities — a West Virginia internal UCC report warning of a runaway reaction was not forwarded to the Bhopal plant despite design similarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure incident lessons and internal safety findings are shared across operations and enforced by regulators; anti-pattern: siloed knowledge and regulatory inaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation and restitution to victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Victims should receive timely, fair compensation — the article documents compensation awards, average family payments, and the 1989 settlement of US$470 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensation programs should be transparent, adequate relative to harm, and timely; anti-pattern: settlements that are delayed, inadequate, or obscure in distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate humanitarian and long-term support
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporations should provide immediate aid and long-term community support — UCC provided emergency aid, contributed funds for a hospital and vocational center, and established relief funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure corporate response by both immediate relief and sustained investment in health, remediation, and livelihoods; anti-pattern: one-off donations without durable commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety culture and worker relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations must foster a safety culture where workers can report issues without punishment — the text notes workers were fined for refusing to deviate from regulations and one employee was fired after a hunger strike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage and protect whistleblowers, avoid retaliation, and engage workers in safety decisions; anti-pattern: penalizing compliance or dissent, eroding trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical engagement with civil society and activists
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporations should engage ethically with activists and journalists — the article reports surveillance of activists and journalists by contracted intelligence services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid surveillance or intimidation; instead maintain transparent dialogue and respect rights to advocacy and reporting; anti-pattern: hiring firms to spy on critics.
